articles.title: Israelis go to the polls with Netanyahu's political survival on the line
articles.summary: By Steven Scheer and Pesha Magid JERUSALEM, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Israelis surged to the polls at the fastest rate in 45 years on Tuesday, passing wartime judgment on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in what voters described as the most consequential election in their history. In the first election since the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks, voters are passionately engaged over the trauma of the country's deadliest day, ‌and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Policies of Netanyahu's right-wing coalition have been divisive at home and have deepened Israel's international isolation, but he has defended his record as the only leader ‌with the mettle to face Israel's foes. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader with 19 years in office, is an unmatched political survivor, and his nationalist politics are increasingly entrenched. Israel's fragmented system makes it difficult for an array of opponents to force out his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox ​parties. His main rival Gadi Eisenkot, a military ex-chief of staff and security hawk, aims to unseat him with the support of parties on the right and centre, as well as the rump of an increasingly marginalised left. Opinion polls show a close race, with neither leader facing an easy path to power. Voters began casting ballots after polling stations opened at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT). The polls close at 10 p.m. (2000 GMT). The Central Elections Committee reported that 16.7% of eligible voters had already cast their ballots within the first three hours, the fastest early turnout rate since 1981. "I think these elections are the most important of all the ones I’ve known," said Ruth Epstein, an 81-year-old longtime left-wing voter in Ramat Gan near Tel Aviv, who ‌voted for the opposition Democrats. "I’m really scared about what will be here." Netanyahu supporter Louis ⁠Lipsky of Jerusalem said he was voting to keep the prime minister in power, crediting him with normalising relations with several Arab states under the Abraham Accords of 2020. Netanyahu has campaigned on his wartime leadership and an endorsement from US President Donald Trump, his ally in war against Iran, who has said they should "finish the job". If neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot ⁠can form a governing coalition in the 120-seat parliament, Netanyahu could stay on as caretaker until another election is held. His opponents have managed to wrest him from the premiership only once since 2009, and that took four inconclusive elections in two years. He was back 18 months later. EISENKOT SEES 'NEW SPIRIT' For many of Netanyahu's opponents, the election turns on accountability for the security failures of October 7, Israel's deadliest day. Opposition groups have promised to hold a national inquiry, which Netanyahu's government has resisted. "I am convinced that ​by ​the end of today, we will see a change — a new spirit for the State of Israel — that will serve as a ​rectification for the past three years and for that terrible day," Eisenkot said during a ‌visit to kibbutz Nir Oz in southern Israel, targeted in the October 7 attacks. He walked to the polls with Gadi Mozes, one of 251 people kidnapped by Hamas and taken to Gaza during the attack that killed 1,200 people. Eisenkot says Israel's response — a war which health authorities say killed more than 74,000 Palestinians — was a failure because Hamas remains in charge. He repeated his commitment to dismantle or destroy Hamas' military and governing power in Gaza within 18 months of forming a government. In his first public commentary on election day, Netanyahu shared an article on X about an incident in which police said three people were arrested over an election bribery attempt. "Right-wing voters, dear Likud voters, in the face of attempts to undermine the integrity of the elections, we must go out and vote en masse, vote Likud for the sake of our country," he said. Netanyahu's critics have said the prime minister may try to cast doubt on ‌the integrity of the voting process, which his office rejects. Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of a far-right party in Netanyahu's coalition, cast his vote ​in the Kiryat Arba settlement in the occupied West Bank early on Tuesday. He predicted Netanyahu would return as prime minister and his ​own party would serve as the right-wing anchor of the government. ARAB TURNOUT COULD BE KEY Voters from Israel's Arab ​minority — Israeli by citizenship but Palestinian by heritage — were voting in "unprecedented"  numbers, Palestinian candidate Ahmed Tibi said. Eisenkot has ruled out partnering with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values, although ‌some experts envision them propping up a minority government to ensure Netanyahu is removed from ​office. "My expectation is that we will have only a slight ​majority either way. No landslide," said Israeli political analyst Amotz Asa-El of the Shalom Hartman Institute. THE WARTIME RECORD Eisenkot joined Netanyahu's war cabinet after the October 7 attacks but quit after eight months, criticising his leadership. Israel flattened much of Gaza in the offensive launched after October 7, and now occupies around two-thirds of the enclave under a year-old US-brokered ceasefire. Israel also dealt heavy blows to Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon and traded strikes ​with Iran, culminating in a 12-day aerial campaign against Iranian nuclear sites in 2025 ‌and this year's joint US-Israeli war. Like nearly all Jewish-led parties in Israel, Eisenkot opposes the two-state solution that underpinned decades of peace negotiations with the Palestinians. But he has criticised Jewish settler violence against ​Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, which has surged since 2023 and strained Israel's ties with Western states. And he opposes Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners. (Additional reporting by Maayan Lubell and Rami Ayyub ​in Jerusalem and Lili Bayer in Tel Aviv; Writing by Tom Perry; Editing by Howard Goller, Joe Bavier, Peter Graff) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/netanyahus-political-survival-line-israel-000240854.html

articles.title: 2 men charged over suspected Iran-linked plot at U.S. bomber base in England
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — Two men were charged Tuesday with national security offenses over a suspected plot against RAF Fairford, a U.S.-run military air base in England, police and prosecutors said. British nationals Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim and Nouman Essghir, both aged 24 and from London, were charged under the National Security Act, the Crown Prosecution Service said. They are due to appear in court later Tuesday. Abdulkarim is charged with assisting Iran's intelligence service and Essghir with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the U.K. RAF Fairford, in western England, has been used by American bombers to strike Iran during this year’s war. Essghir was arrested outside the base on Sept. 27, when armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts swarmed the rural area. Scores of residents were evacuated from their homes as police and army bomb-disposal experts searched for explosives. Police later said they had found a quantity of an accelerant — gasoline — in vans at the scene, but no explosives. Essghir was initially released on bail before being re-arrested last week. Abdulkarim was arrested in the past week. Six other men have been arrested and released on bail as investigations continue. British authorities have linked Tehran to the incident, which led the U.S. to pull its bombers from RAF Fairford. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the apparent plot was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard. Iran has denied involvement, although it has previously said that it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target . Earlier this month, the head of Britain’s MI5 spy agency warned that both Iran and Russia were expanding their attacks against the U.K., and that the RAF Fairford incident was not unique. Ken McCallum, who leads the U.K.’s domestic security service, said Tehran is seeking to intensify its attacks in Britain beyond the traditional targets of Iranians opposed to the country’s Islamic authorities. He said more than 50 people have been arrested over Iran-linked plots in the past year. “We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state, and as the director general of MI5 said just the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat,” said Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, the head of National Counter Terrorism Policing in the U.K. ___ A previous version of this story incorrectly said Abdulkarim is a British-Iranian national. He is British. This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/uk-prosecutors-2-men-charged-091007409.html

articles.title: DOJ makes a 3rd run at James Comey using a rarely seen legal tactic
articles.summary: The Justice Department took steps to charge James Comey with leaking classified information earlier this month, court records show, in its third attempt to bring criminal charges against the former FBI director and Trump foe. Prosecutors are seeking to charge Comey with two counts of violating the Espionage Act by transmitting national defense information to a person not entitled to receive it. He has not been indicted by a grand jury or charged by criminal complaint, and was instead targeted through a criminal information filing. In this case, the information was filed in order to preserve the statute of limitations before it expires, according to a Justice Department spokesperson. The official added that "this is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further." A criminal information does not require approval by a grand jury, or a finding by a magistrate judge of probable cause that there is evidence to establish that a crime was committed. Comey's attorney, Patrick Fitzgerald, said Comey "steadfastly maintains his innocence." The latest effort by the Justice Department stems from allegations that Comey gave national defense information to an unnamed individual for disclosure in a newspaper in October 2016. According to court filings in the case, The New York Times published an article on Oct. 5, 2016, titled, "Yahoo Said to Have Aided U.S. Email Surveillance By Adapting Spam Filter." The article cited two unnamed government officials who spoke on the condition of anonymity. The Justice Department alleges that it has uncovered evidence that Comey sought to "correct misinformation which had appeared in the press by way of Reuters the day before" and that Comey "directed staff" to speak with the Times reporter about the accuracy of the Reuters article. Fitzgerald said the information "purports to charge Mr. Comey with crimes that he did not commit," adding that investigators looked into the matter twice during the first Trump administration and "determined that no charges should be brought against anyone." In a separate video statement, Comey said, "well, they're back again" — a reference to the two prior attempts to charge Comey, including a dismissed indictment accusing him of lying to Congress and a still-pending indictment accusing him of threatening President Trump via a social media post of a photo of seashells arranged to say "86 47." "It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice, one that we cannot become numb to," Comey said. "Nothing's changed with me. I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary." Asked about the case late Monday, Mr. Trump told reporters he'd "just heard about it." "I think he's a dirty cop, James Comey, but I know nothing about it," the president said. In a statement posted to social media , the Justice Department said: "Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals." Former prosecutors and defense attorneys told CBS News they had not seen a criminal information filed in a felony case in this manner before, and called the maneuver highly unusual. The practice had been approved in other federal appellate court districts in some cases, but is less common in Washington, D.C. Greg Rosen, a former federal prosecutor who helped lead Jan. 6 cases, told CBS News: "In years of practicing in D.C., I never saw one used this way, let alone in the third attempt by the same Department to charge the same man." Michael Bromwich, a former Justice Department inspector general who is now a defense attorney, told CBS News that he has never encountered a situation where a criminal information was filed to pause the statute of limitations. Normally, such charging documents are filed when a defendant plans to waive their right to have a grand jury weigh charges and opts to plead guilty. "I have never heard of proceeding by information to toll the statute of limitations. Most prosecutors you have ever dealt with have never heard of that. This seems to be a way to do an end-run around the statute of limitations and keep a case alive that deserved to die 9 years ago," Bromwich said. "This is just absolutely bizarro world stuff." DOJ and Comey fought in secret over charging efforts The criminal information were filed under seal in early October, and were unsealed by U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden on Monday at Comey's request. For much of this month, Comey's attorneys and federal prosecutors waged a behind-the-scenes fight over whether the Justice Department's effort to charge him should be dismissed. In an Oct. 9 court filing, Comey's legal team argued the government "filed a faulty information under seal … in an effort to toll the applicable statute of limitations." The crime that the government is seeking to charge Comey under has a 10-year statute of limitations, which would run out in October of this year — but the ex-FBI director's lawyers say the statute of limitations applies to indictments and can't be extended if the government files a criminal information. They also said Comey had "reason to believe that the government plans to use that information to seek an arrest warrant as soon as today, which could result in an after-hours arrest that would ensure Mr. Comey sits in jail over a holiday weekend." "Mr. Comey has reason to believe multiple federal law enforcement officers have surveilled his whereabouts while traveling to a family members' residence and around his own neighborhood throughout the week," Comey's lawyers wrote on Oct. 9, just before Columbus Day weekend. In an emergency court hearing, the government agreed to hold off on seeking an indictment for 30 days, attorneys for Comey later wrote . The Justice Department argued that Comey's efforts to dismiss the criminal information was premature because no indictment has been returned. "This is not the proper time for him to file pretrial motions or attempt to chip away at charging documents before he subjects himself to the Court's jurisdiction," the government said. Further, the department said the law allows the government to proceed because it permits prosecutors to meet the deadline if the "indictment is found or the information is instituted." In an unusual move, the criminal information filed by the department were signed by two senior officials — acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter and Principal Associate Deputy Attorney General Aakash Singh — as well as several special assistant U.S. attorneys who are not originally from the U.S. Attorney's office in Washington, D.C. McFadden, the Trump-nominated judge overseeing the case, ordered the court docket to be unsealed Monday, writing: "Criminal charges against a former FBI director for his conduct while in office are of significant public interest." He also said Comey "is aware of the criminal information and has offered to 'self-surrender,'" so there is no need to keep the case secret in order to help the government apprehend him. The judge did not rule on the merits of the case. Two prior investigations into FBI leaks This is not the first time that the Justice Department has sought to investigate the disclosure of classified information in connection with a 2016 Times article. Former U.S. Attorney John Durham of Connecticut, who was later appointed special counsel by Attorney General William Barr, investigated the matter in 2017, according to court filings in the case from Comey's defense team . At the time, he determined there were two sources for the article, including James Baker, the former FBI general counsel. As part of that investigation, Baker said the FBI's chief of staff instructed him to provide the information and he understood it was being conveyed at Comey's instruction. Durham ultimately did not recommend Baker or anyone else for prosecution. Baker could not be immediately reached for comment. The matter was later investigated a second time — in that case by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia under an investigation code-named Tropic Vortex. That was closed in February 2020, also without charges, according to court papers . Comey and Trump The Justice Department filed the criminal information in early October, about a month before the midterm elections. It marks the latest overt investigative step taken by the Justice Department in a politically charged case, a maneuver that runs counter to longstanding norms. Mr. Trump and Comey have had a contentious relationship for nearly a decade, dating back to when the president fired the former FBI chief early in his first term. His firing is what prompted then-Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein to appoint Special Counsel Robert Mueller, whose investigation dogged Mr. Trump for much of his first term. The two have exchanged barbs since then, with Mr. Trump calling Comey a "dirty cop" and repeatedly arguing he should be prosecuted , while Comey called Mr. Trump "morally unfit" to be president. In September 2025, the Justice Department obtained an indictment against Comey that charged him with lying to Congress, alleging he falsely told lawmakers in a 2020 hearing that he had never authorized an FBI employee to serve as an anonymous source. The indictment was personally signed by Lindsey Halligan, a former Trump White House aide who had been sworn in as interim U.S. attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia days earlier. Beforehand, staff in that office circulated a memo that argued charges should not be brought against Comey, CBS News has previously reported . A judge dismissed the charges on the grounds that Halligan was improperly appointed. Then, in April of this year, Comey was indicted in North Carolina on allegations that he threatened to kill Mr. Trump by posting to Instagram a photo of seashells arranged to form the numbers "86 47." (Mr. Trump is the 47th president.) Comey has long denied wrongdoing, and his attorneys have argued the charges against him are politically motivated. They are currently seeking to have the North Carolina charges dismissed on several grounds, including that his prosecution is vindictive and selective. That matter is currently pending. Comey isn't the only Trump foe to face criminal scrutiny. New York Attorney General Letitia James was also charged by Halligan's office with bank fraud last year. Her indictment was tossed out along with the first Comey indictment. Prosecutors presented her case to grand juries at least twice after that, but the grand jurors declined to re-indict her . Attorney General Todd Blanche has long denied that the charges against Comey and other Trump adversaries are driven by politics. In an interview with CBS News earlier this year, he said the "86 47" indictment was driven by "local prosecutors" and "local agents." Asked if Mr. Trump has called him up and ordered him to prosecute certain individuals, Blanche told CBS News he wouldn't discuss his conversations with the president, but "rest assured, he has much better, bigger and important things to do than to worry about me doing my job." articles.title: Judge halts tree cutting at Trump's golf course renovation after 400-plus trees removed
articles.summary: A golfer walks in front of cut down trees at East Potomac Golf Links near Hains Point in Washington, DC, October 19, 2026. - Saul Loeb/AFP/Getty Images A federal judge extended an order blocking tree removal from a Washington, DC golf course President Donald Trump is seeking to renovate, while imposing new notice requirements on any other major changes the administration seeks to make on the golf course grounds. The new 70-page opinion from US District Judge Ana Reyes cited Trump’s own statements about his plans for East Potomac Golf Course. The judge said she was forced to act now in the long-simmering dispute – which came to a head in recent weeks because the administration cut down 400-plus trees on the grounds with little notice – “because the Government did what it assured all it would not do.” The ruling is a major setback for Trump’s efforts to turn the beloved but modest public golf course into a championship level course. It also sets the stage for an appeals court battle in a case that had produced sharp confrontations between the administration and the judiciary. The new ruling comes after a showdown between the Trump administration and the federal bench in DC during a marathon hearing last week over the president’s efforts to overhaul the course. Tensions were ratcheted up for those proceedings when Trump posted to social media that construction would begin at the course “immediately,” while calling Reyes a “crazed lunatic.” “The events surrounding this case have become extraordinary,” Reyes wrote Monday. The way the Trump administration rushed to chop down hundreds of trees was “concerning,” she said. “The Government appears to have set the timing of the tree removal and late notice to impede Plaintiffs’ ability to seek Court intervention,” Reyes wrote. “And its recent actions call into question other representations it has made to the Court over these many months.” Reyes said she was reserving judgment on whether the government purposely misled her. But she indicated she is considering issuing a preservation order for all DOJ communications regarding the tree removal – a signal she may further probe the conduct of the government’s attorneys. Under Reyes’ order, the administration cannot take any action to cut down, alter or harm additional trees on the grounds – unless to protect public safety, and in those cases, it must give detailed notice to the court. The Trump administration must also give 10 days notice for any plans to close the golf course or if it plans to make “irreversible” alterations to the course’s design, Reyes said. Just before midnight Monday, Trump railed on Truth Social about Reyes’ ruling, while continuing to vow he will close the course on November 15 to renovate it. “The judge does not have the Constitutional Right to ‘ask for or receive notices,’ which are time-consuming, unnecessary, expensive, and unconstitutional. We will immediately appeal this decision,” Trump said in the post. “To have to give advanced notices to a judge who has no expertise in Golf, Architecture, Landscaping, Construction, or anything else having to do with building such a World Class Project, is not fair, appropriate, or Constitutional.” The lawsuit was brought by historic preservationists and individual golfers who alleged the administration was violating environmental law in how it planned to carry out Trump’s wishes to renovate East Potomac Golf Course – which for decades has offered affordable golf access to DC residents. Trump’s plans for the course would likely make it far more difficult to access and expensive to play, while eliminating much of the public park space that surrounds it. The new decision stems from the October 10 move by the administration to chop down hundreds of trees from the grounds. In the months and even days before the mass tree removal, administration officials had claimed that the proposals for Trump’s renovation were still in their infancy, and there were no imminent plans for making major changes to the course. After chopping down more than 400 trees, the administration continued to argue that the tree removals were separate from the overhaul Trump was planning and were instead the product of a 2019 proposal to make the course look more like it did when it was first built. Reyes had expressed deep skepticism of that explanation. She had initially issued a temporary restraining order blocking all tree removal and requiring three days’ notice of any other major changes to the course. That TRO was set to expire on Monday. In her latest opinion, Reyes concluded that she would trust Trump’s own public statements that renovations were beginning “immediately” over what government officials had claimed in court. The Justice Department, she wrote, “asks the Court to disbelieve repeated public comments made by the President, who has stated in no uncertain terms that DOI and Secretary Burgum have a plan to redesign the Course.” Reyes devoted a significant portion of her opinion Monday to defending the judiciary’s ability to serve as a check on the executive branch. “One branch may not shield itself from accountability merely by invoking separation of powers principles without any reasoning. But that is all the Government has done,” she wrote. This story has been updated with additional details. articles.title: Convicted murderer flees in stolen truck after escaping Tennessee prison
articles.summary: This booking photo released by the Tennessee Department of Correction on July 24, 2025, shows Jacob Morley. - Tennessee Department of Correction/AP A 28-year-old convicted murderer serving a life sentence escaped through a Tennessee prison’s fence Sunday evening before stealing a truck and driving off — and has not yet been located, according to Tennessee authorities. Around 11:30 p.m. on October 25, staff at the Northwest Correctional Complex learned Jacob Morley was missing, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. He had been sentenced to life in prison after being convicted of first-degree murder, aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism. Security camera footage later revealed Morley “breached the perimeter fence” and left the facility wearing his prison uniform, the department said. It remains unclear how he escaped through the fence. Video obtained by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation shows Morley stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350 with Tennessee plates around 1 a.m. on October 26, the agency said. unknown content item - The Hornbeak Fire Department , which is about 15 miles from the Northwest Correctional Complex, said it captured video of Morley passing in front of the fire department building in the stolen truck around 1:18 a.m. Morley is the second inmate to escape from the Tennessee Department of Correction’s custody in the past week. Morley was convicted of first-degree murder for the killing of Cody Birchfield, who was initially reported missing in February 2022, according to the Carter County Sheriff’s Office. Birchfield’s body was found in a box under Morley’s house weeks after he went missing, The Associated Press reported. Morley also led police on a chase that ended in North Carolina after he found deputies at his home in 2022, according to authorities. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, which has added Morley to its “Most Wanted” list, is offering a reward of up to $2,500 for information leading to his arrest. The Northwest Correctional Complex can house up to 1,776 male inmates, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction . CNN’s Amanda Jackson contributed to this report. articles.title: Ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump goes into effect in Russian-occupied town
articles.summary: Smoke rises from a residential neighborhood in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region of Ukraine in a video the Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine Brigade released Sept. 22. (Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine Brigade / via AP) A rare humanitarian ceasefire brokered by first lady Melania Trump to save people trapped in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian town went into effect early Tuesday. After months of warnings from Ukrainian officials about an unraveling humanitarian catastrophe in the front-line town of Oleshky, in the southern Kherson region, the White House announced last week that the first lady had secured a pause in the fighting. The agreement would “temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway,” it said. Hours after it began at 3 a.m. local time (9 p.m. ET Monday), the ceasefire appeared to be holding, with the two sides conducting attacks elsewhere but not in Oleshky. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Tuesday there have been no reports of violations so far. Hours after the truce came into effect, Russian President Vladimir Putin held a phone call with the leaders of Norway and Finland about ending the war in Ukraine — a rare instance of direct talks between the Russian leader and European leaders, whom the Kremlin has accused of prolonging the conflict by supporting Kyiv. Neither side has indicated when the temporary ceasefire would end. “An important humanitarian mission has begun in Oleshky. A bilateral ceasefire has been declared in the area where the mission is taking place,” the head of the Ukrainian president’s office, Kyrylo Budanov, said Tuesday in a post on X. The Russian Defense Ministry said in a statement that its forces had ceased firing at the agreed time “in connection with preparations for a humanitarian operation” in Oleshky. Destroyed cars on a highway from Oleshky on Sept. 30. (Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen" via AP) The rare humanitarian agreement comes amid renewed pressure from President Donald Trump on Kyiv to agree to a deal to end the war, which began when Russia ⁠invaded Ukraine in February 2022. Ukraine complained of gaps in intelligence sharing from the U.S. and a slowdown of Elon Musk’s Starlink service , both of which it says have now been restored. It has also said the U.S. is holding up supplies of crucial interceptor missiles. Earlier this month, Trump also agreed to a deal allowing Russia to supply diesel to the global market, in an apparent bid to lower prices ahead of the midterm elections. The move, and his later waiving of sanctions, reversed years of American policy and raised alarm in Ukraine and Europe. But in a rare intervention from the first lady, the White House quoted her as saying last week that Oleshky was “on the brink of disaster” and its remaining population, composed primarily of elderly residents, was in urgent need of medical attention, medicine, food and clean water. “The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks,” she said. “It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.” Civilian representatives from both sides will visit the town, which had a population of around 24,000 people before the war, to determine the level of assistance the remaining residents require, the statement said. An “impartial American media organization” will document the process to ensure “that the wishes of each family are faithfully respected,” it added. Both sides blame each other for the crisis in Oleshky. Kyiv has accused Russian forces of mining nearby roads and using the remaining residents as human shields to prevent Ukraine’s army from conducting offensive operations in the town. Meanwhile, Russia has blamed Ukraine for “laying siege to the town” with drone strikes and preventing humanitarian aid from getting in. Last month, the Kremlin acknowledged problems with food and medical ​supplies getting into Oleshky, saying its military was working to resolve them. Ukrainian media has for months been featuring interviews with people who have managed to escape Oleshky and spoken to relatives of those who remain there — an estimated 2,000 people, including children. Some said the town was on the verge of starvation and residents were relying on homegrown produce to survive. Others had reportedly resorted to eating grass. With winter looming, fears of famine are growing in the town where communication is difficult because of a severely compromised internet and cellphone service in the area. The United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine, which has been documenting the crisis for months, said there have been no food deliveries to the town since the end of May. The ceasefire is likely to last several days as the Russian side has to “clear the roads of mines,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an interview with Ukraine’s TSN TV channel Sunday, adding that his forces would have to verify the area is clear. “There is no doubt that Russia will do everything it can to clear the roads of mines so that these people head toward Russia and stay there. They are not going to simply let people go,” he said. Oleshky, like a large portion of the Kherson region, has been occupied by Russian forces since the early weeks of the invasion. Drone footage of the town, shared by Ukraine’s 34th Separate Marine Brigade “Borysfen” last month and verified by NBC News, shows the charred ruins of desolate residential and administrative buildings inside the town, in a rare look at the level of destruction. Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, shared another video earlier this month, geolocated by NBC News, showing residents leaving Oleshky on foot, bicycles and mopeds in what he said was a desperate search for food. He said they faced the impossible choice of being blown up on a mine or dying from hunger. Their plight received international attention in recent weeks after Pope Leo XIV directly raised the growing crisis with Putin, and European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno went on a hunger strike, saying “the people of Oleshky cannot be abandoned.” While both Kyiv and Moscow have unilaterally announced Easter or Christmas ceasefires before, they did not revolve around a humanitarian crisis and have not involved open mediation by the U.S., making the Oleshky ceasefire an unprecedented halting of fire between the two sides. The ceasefire could serve as a model for similar humanitarian arrangements in other areas, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday, especially given the “highly positive” American involvement, including from the first lady. Melania Trump has been involved in the humanitarian campaign to bring back Ukrainian children taken by Russia , and the White House statement said she leveraged the “communication channel” established through those efforts to bring about a humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky. articles.title: Court rejects DOJ's emergency bid to separate Calif. ballots over noncitizen claims
articles.summary: A federal appeals court has rejected the Trump administration's late-breaking effort to force California to separate mail-in ballots from 20,000 purported noncitizens. A 2-1 ruling from a panel of the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals concluded that the Justice Department improperly circumvented a lower-court judge who had scheduled a hearing on the matter on Tuesday and moved too slowly to seek emergency relief. “[T]he United States failed to allow the district court adequate opportunity to consider its application for a Temporary Restraining Order,” the majority wrote. “The United States’s claimed emergency, at least in part, is a self-constructed one.” Judge Mark Bennett, a Trump appointee, joined Judge Gabriel Sanchez, a Biden appointee, in turning down the administration’s emergency appeal. Judge Patrick Bumatay, another Trump appointee, dissented and said he would have granted the request. Though the outcome was foreshadowed in a hearing Sunday in which the judges appeared skeptical of their power to take up the Trump administration’s case, the dissent by Bumatay created a surprising split. Bumatay said the Trump administration’s view — that a federal criminal law barring voting by noncitizens superseded California’s election procedures — would likely prevail in the end, and that every day without relief from the courts increased the likelihood that noncitizens' votes would be improperly counted in the midterm elections. “The question—does the federal government have the power to stop this potential attack on the integrity of our elections?” Bumatay wrote. “Under both federal law and the Constitution, the answer must be “yes.” Simply, the federal government has a sovereign interest in safeguarding federal elections and ensuring that the votes of noncitizens do not undermine our electoral results.” In a separate concurrence, Bennett rebutted Bumatay’s position, arguing that the Justice Department would likely fail on the substance of its lawsuit. Bennett said the Trump administration “has offered no workable plan of any kind as to how the remedy it seeks could be accomplished in practice without potential catastrophic consequences to California’s ongoing election.” California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat and 2028 presidential contender, called the ruling “a positive development and a welcome speed bump to Trump's disgusting attacks on the Constitution and our country's democracy.” “Trump is illegally trying to seize powers in the Constitution entrusted to others so he can stay in power,” Newsom said in a statement. “This lawsuit is just the latest step.” U.S. District Judge David Carter, a Clinton appointee, has scheduled a hearing on the Trump administration’s restraining order request for Tuesday afternoon in Los Angeles. The Trump administration had the opportunity to ask a larger group of 9th Circuit judges to take up the appeal, but did not do so before a deadline the court set. The appeals court formally released the case back to Carter Monday night, allowing him to proceed with his hearing as planned. The Justice Department could still file an emergency appeal with the Supreme Court or launch a new round of appeals if Carter turns down the administration’s request. A Justice Department spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment. articles.title: Man charged with sending suspicious substance to 4 members of Congress
articles.summary: The case began after an anonymous online tipster told the FBI that they overheard the man talking about mailing a suspicious substance to members of Congress. (Graeme Sloan / Bloomberg via Getty) WASHINGTON — A man has been charged in Illinois with mailing four letters containing a white granular substance to members of Congress , all of which were sent in envelopes bearing his name and home address. Matthew Unglesbee has been charged with sending threatening letters containing a white granular substance to three members of Congress, along with a handwritten letter that read “HA HA.” A fourth letter with a white granular substance included the note “HAH enjoy the gift.” Unglesbee faces two charges: false information and hoaxes and mailing threatening communications. He will make an initial appearance in court Monday afternoon. A letter received by the district office of a member of Congress on Wednesday with a white granular substance spilling from the unopened envelope. The photo has been redacted for privacy. (U.S. District Court) In an interview with FBI personnel Sunday, Unglesbee is alleged to have admitted that he mailed four letters to four members of Congress after he heard about other letters mailed earlier in the month . The FBI is separately investigating letters containing suspicious substances that were sent to members of Congress and elections officials in recent weeks. Unglesbee admitted that he knew that people would perceive the letters as dangerous, the FBI said. He said in the FBI interview that the granular substance was salt, which he said “kind of looks like” anthrax, authorities said. He denied involvement with prior mailings, they said. Rep. Jan Schakowsky, D-Ill., said Monday she was “aware of reports that a suspect has been taken into custody in connection with the most recent suspicious letter sent” to her district office. The congresswoman received a second suspicious letter on Oct. 21. “I’m aware of reports that a suspect has been taken into custody in connection with the most recent suspicious letter sent to my Skokie office,” she said in a statement thanking law enforcement. “I will not let threats stand in the way of serving the people of the 9th District. My community relies on the services our office provides, and my team and I will continue doing the work I was elected to do.” A search of Unglesbee’s residence turned up a fifth unmailed and empty envelope that was addressed to a member of Congress, according to the FBI. The case began after an anonymous online tipster told the FBI that they overheard Unglesbee talking about mailing a suspicious substance to members of Congress. The tip was received on Oct. 16, and the FBI responded when the letters showed up at the offices of members of Congress three days later. articles.title: Dollar General accused of overcharging shoppers in lawsuit filed by FTC and 20 states
articles.summary: By Jody Godoy Oct 26 (Reuters) - Dollar General repeatedly charged more than advertised prices even after ‌receiving tens of thousands of consumer complaints, ‌the US Federal Trade Commission and 20 states alleged in a ​lawsuit filed on Monday. Dollar General, which appeals to low-income consumers with bargain prices, made millions of dollars by failing to honor prices advertised on fliers and ‌shelves at checkout, ⁠the FTC and states allege. The discount retailer's stock was down more than 4% on ⁠Monday afternoon. "Dollar General has, for years, repeatedly mislabeled prices, overcharged consumers and failed to correct the issue ​despite extensive ​corporate knowledge of the ​problem," the FTC and ‌states said in a statement. Representatives for Dollar General did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lawsuit cited numerous complaints from consumers, failed inspections conducted by state authorities, and undercover shopping sprees conducted ‌by the FTC. Portions of the ​lawsuit detailing the company's knowledge ​of the practices ​were largely redacted. California joined the FTC ‌lawsuit along with Florida, Illinois, ​Michigan, Ohio, North ​Carolina, Tennessee and 13 other states. Since 2019, Dollar General has paid $6 million in settlements with ​six states over ‌inaccurate pricing, according to the complaint. articles.title: “这种模式我们见过！”大空头交易员详解：为何做空AI新贵CoreWeave
articles.summary: 因《大空头》一书和电影而声名大噪的交易员们，正将目光瞄准AI算力租赁公司CoreWeave。 由三位"大空头"交易员联合创立的投资机构Seawolf Capital公开宣布做空CoreWeave，并系统阐述了其看空逻辑——这家公司的商业模式似曾相识，而资本获取能力才是真正的致命软肋。 Seawolf联合创始人Vincent Daniel在一篇Substack文章中披露， 该机构已建立CoreWeave空头头寸，并将其商业模式与多家资产租赁公司进行类比 。他指出，GPU的经济寿命可能远不及石油钻井平台、飞机或航运设备，而竞争性芯片供给正在以惊人速度扩张，这使CoreWeave的护城河存在根本性疑问。 Daniel强调，这一空头押注的核心逻辑并非看空AI行业整体前景，而是对资本可得性与融资成本的判断。他认为，科技公司正与政府争夺融资资源，叠加货币政策收紧周期， CoreWeave若无法以低廉成本持续融资，其商业模式将难以为继 。CoreWeave股价近期已因债务问题引发市场担忧而出现明显下跌。 从一条社交媒体帖子到系统性做空 Seawolf的CoreWeave空头头寸，起源于一个颇具戏剧性的契机。 Daniel表示，此前有人在X平台上嘲讽那些做空CoreWeave却缺乏财务分析支撑的投资者，这反而促使Seawolf团队决定认真研究这家公司。 "很难反驳这种说法，所以我们决定认真研究一番，"Daniel写道。" 当我们深入挖掘CoreWeave的故事时，开始意识到它的商业模式看起来非常熟悉。" Daniel与Seawolf联合创始人Danny Moses、Porter Collins共同对CoreWeave展开深度研究。CoreWeave的核心业务是租赁以英伟达GPU为主的高性能AI算力，属于所谓"新云"（neocloud）赛道。 "这种模式我们见过"：与传统资产租赁公司的类比 Seawolf将CoreWeave的商业模式与多家传统资产租赁公司进行了对比，包括向石油公司租赁钻井平台的Transocean，以及航空设备租赁公司AerCap Holdings。 值得注意的是， Seawolf同时持有上述两家公司的头寸，但明确表示更倾向于这两家，而非CoreWeave。 原因在于资产的经济寿命与供给约束存在本质差异。Daniel指出，Seawolf偏好租赁那些底层供给受到结构性约束、远期订单规模有限的资产。"尽管算力需求无疑十分旺盛，但竞争性芯片产能的远期供给正在以惊人速度扩张。"相比之下，GPU的经济寿命存在更大的不确定性。 资本结构是核心风险 在财务层面，Seawolf的担忧更为具体。Daniel指出，CoreWeave的运营需要持续大规模采购高价AI芯片，资本消耗极为密集。 "基于预计2027年的自由现金流缺口以及当前资产负债表的杠杆水平（具体而言是有形普通股权益与总资产之比），这一局面令人望而生畏，" Daniel写道。"要持有这只股票，投资者必须相信CoreWeave能够以增值条件筹集数百亿美元的增量资本——这不是我们愿意押注的赌局。" 他同时坦承，Seawolf目前对CoreWeave的分析仍处于"早期阶段"。 与WeWork的类比，以及对AI大局的判断 这并非Seawolf首次公开质疑CoreWeave。本月早些时候，Moses曾在"The Real Eisman Playbook"节目中与另一位"大空头"投资者Steve Eisman同台，将CoreWeave比作WeWork——这家曾经的硅谷办公空间独角兽如今已成为科技创业公司的警示案例。 不过，Daniel明确区分了这一空头押注与对AI行业整体的判断。他表示，Seawolf的CoreWeave空头本质上是对资本可得性和融资成本的押注：科技公司正与政府争夺融资资源，货币政策收紧周期进一步压缩了廉价融资空间。 "如果它无法以低廉成本融资，或者资本根本无法获得，那么走完这段路将会非常艰难——这正是我对CoreWeave所做的判断，"Daniel对Business Insider表示。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 25.83万亿元，私募基金规模又创历史新高！
articles.summary: 中国证券投资基金业协会（后简称中基协）发布最新数据显示，截至 9 月末，私募基金管理规模升至 25.83 万亿元，较 8 月末继续扩张， 这不仅是年内又一次创下新高，也意味着私募证券投资基金继续成为中国资本市场的增量资金来源之一。 私募证券基金成增长来源 中基协数据显示，截至 2026 年 9 月末，存续私募基金管理人 18398 家，管理基金数量 145712 只，管理总规模 25.83 万亿元，均创下历史新高。 其中，私募证券投资基金管理人 7172 家；私募股权、创业投资基金管理人 11064 家；私募资产配置类基金管理人 3 家；其他私募投资基金管理人 159 家。 对比上月数据：私募证券投资基金管理人从 8 月末的 7203 家降至 7172 家，管理人数量继续减少；而证券类私募的管理规模逆势上行，成为拉动全行业规模增长的主要动力。 这意味着行业正走向管理规模稳步扩张，行业整体提质增效的良好趋势。 优势地区持续集聚 拉长时间来看，今年 1 月末行业总规模仅 22.44 万亿元，截至 9 月末年内累计新增规模 3.39 万亿元，行业稳步增长大趋势鲜明。 另外，今年以来 私募基金区域布局集聚效应显著。 截至 2026 年 9 月末（按 36 个辖区统计），管理人主要集中在上海、北京、深圳、浙江（除宁波）、广东（除深圳）、江苏六地 ，上述地域 合计占 全国市场的 72.37% ，相比 8 月份的 72.35% 小幅抬升。 各地管理人数量：上海 3508 家（ 19.07% ）、北京 3068 家（ 16.68% ）、深圳 2665 家（ 14.49% ）、浙江（除宁波） 1469 家（ 7.98% ）、广东（除深圳） 1463 家（ 7.95% ）、江苏 1142 家（ 6.21% ）。 从管理规模看，集聚特征同样明显，规模前六大辖区与上述地区一致，合计占比 76.01% ，略高于 8 月的 75.98% 。各地管理规模：上海 72109.09 亿元（ 27.91% ）、北京 60131.08 亿元（ 23.28% ）、深圳 22854.32 亿元（ 8.85% ）、广东（除深圳） 15028.57 亿元（ 5.82% ）、江苏 14447.57 亿元（ 5.59% ）、浙江（除宁波） 11775.04 亿元（ 4.56% ）。 整体而言，私募基金资源高度向国内金融核心城市集中。上海、北京在机构数量与管理规模上长期领跑，依托完善的金融配套、人才、资金与产业基础形成资管集群；深圳、江浙及广东其他地区紧随其后，依靠科创产业与民营经济，支撑股权创投与证券类私募发展。这一格局是金融要素自然流动的结果，头部金融高地的优势还将持续巩固。 持续发展动力何在？ 那么私募行业的持续发展动力是什么呢？ 一方面，居民和机构的理财偏好正在发生变化，存款、普通理财收益水平相对有限，难以满足多元化的收益需求，不少投资者选择配置私募基金，以追求更好的收益。随着市场活力增强，资金进一步流入证券类私募，为行业发展提供支撑。 与此同时，股权、创投基金持续服务实体经济，为科创、高端制造等领域的企业输送长期发展资金，成为行业规模稳定增长的重要底盘。 此外，随着行业监管持续规范，不合规的机构逐步出清，市场资金更倾向于选择风控扎实、业绩稳健的优质管理人，助推行业走向高质量发展。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 2026年10月27日，四川省成都市中级人民法院一审公开宣判中国证券监督管理委员会原党委委员、中央纪委国家监委驻中国证券监督管理委员会纪检监察组原组长王会民受贿案，对被告人王会民以受贿罪判处死刑，缓期二年执行，剥夺政治权利终身，并处没收个人全部财产，在其死刑缓期执行二年期满依法减为无期徒刑后，终身监禁，不得减刑、假释；对追缴在案的王会民受贿犯罪所得财物及孳息依法上缴国库，不足部分继续追缴。 经审理查明：1998年至2025年，被告人王会民利用担任中国建设银行新疆维吾尔自治区分行行长、党委书记，新疆维吾尔自治区人民政府主席助理，新疆维吾尔自治区人民政府金融工作办公室主任、党组书记，新疆维吾尔自治区农村信用社联合社党委书记，中国证券监督管理委员会纪委书记，中央纪委驻中国证券监督管理委员会纪检组组长等职务上的便利以及职权、地位形成的便利条件，为相关单位和个人在企业经营、募集资金等事项上提供帮助，直接或通过他人非法收受财物共计折合人民币4.36亿余元。 成都市中级人民法院认为，被告人王会民的行为构成受贿罪。王会民受贿数额特别巨大，并使国家和人民利益遭受特别重大损失，论罪应当判处死刑。鉴于其受贿犯罪中有未遂情节；到案后如实供述自己罪行，主动交代办案机关尚未掌握的部分受贿事实；认罪悔罪，受贿赃款部分追缴，具有法定、酌定从宽处罚情节，对其判处死刑，可不立即执行。同时，根据王会民犯罪的事实和情节，决定在其死刑缓期执行二年期满依法减为无期徒刑后，终身监禁，不得减刑、假释。法庭遂作出上述判决。 据悉，成都市中级人民法院于2026年7月17日公开开庭审理了该案。庭审中，检察机关出示了相关证据，被告人王会民及其辩护人进行了质证，控辩双方在法庭的主持下充分发表了意见，王会民进行了最后陈述，并当庭表示认罪悔罪。人大代表、政协委员和各界群众30余人旁听了庭审。 本文来源： 央视新闻 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 港币为什么会被狙击？从联系汇率到稳定币的底层逻辑【胡捷大师课3.5】
articles.summary: 精彩内容预览 全世界的央行使命大同小异，但发行货币的模式不止一种。最特别的一种叫货币局制度，全球只有四个，香港是最有名的那个。 港币的基础货币不是金管局“凭空写”出来的：汇丰、渣打、中银三家发钞行把美元交给外汇基金，换回一张收据，凭收据才能印钞——1比7.8，后面有美元足额支撑。但故事没完：商业银行拿到基础港币后照样“吹牛”，1亿能贷出5亿，派生货币滚滚而来。把派生和基础加在一起去找外汇基金兑美元，是不够兑的——这正是当年狙击港币的逻辑入口：联系汇率在逻辑上存在脱钩的可能。 顺着这条线往下，就是今天的稳定币。上海交通大学高级金融学院、前美联储高级经济学家胡捷一句话点透：稳定币就是“不准做派生”的货币局，收到1美元才能发1个币。早期Tether拿储备去买比特币这类冒险操作，恰恰是监管要堵的漏洞。 从欧央行对希腊“送了一个字：滚”，到中国央行的麻辣粉、酸辣粉，再到蒙代尔不可能三角——本节课程把全球主要货币发行模式一次讲清。????点击 此处 或下方课程表解锁完整内容。

articles.title: 塔塔将接手依维柯，中国商用车出海遇劲敌
articles.summary: 10月27日，塔塔收购依维柯的首轮要约初步结果出炉。接受要约的股份占扣除库存股后普通股本的89.42%，超过交易所需的80%门槛。若最终结果及其余条件得到确认，双方计划于10月30日付款交割。 这笔始于去年7月的收购，正在走到最后阶段。塔塔已将要约价格从每股14.10欧元提高至14.40欧元，按全部股份接受要约计算，最高现金对价约39.06亿欧元。依维柯的军工业务已出售给Leonardo，塔塔将接手的业务包括卡车、客车、FPT动力总成及金融服务。 福田、宇通等中国商用车企业，需要重新审视这位欧洲对手。它们正向欧洲、拉美投入更多资源，而塔塔希望借这笔收购，把印度的采购和研发能力带入依维柯。欧洲品牌原有的产品、工厂和服务网络，可能因此获得更有竞争力的成本。 这种组合，触及了中国商用车出海最重要的一项优势。 塔塔在向投资者解释交易时，提出了共同采购、拓展低成本采购来源，以及合并部分电动化、排放和智能化研发投入的计划。对依维柯来说，零部件采购和新车开发有了更大的调整余地；对塔塔来说，依维柯在欧洲、拉美已经建立的市场位置，则能帮助它扩大海外业务。 塔塔此前主要依托印度市场，并在非洲、中东等地经营。依维柯的业务重心在欧洲，拉美也是其重要市场。并购为双方互用渠道、扩充当地产品线提供了条件。 据《印度时报》今年6月报道，塔塔商用车负责人吉里什·瓦格已提出，利用依维柯分销网络将塔塔卡车引入拉美，并将部分依维柯产品带入印度。这些安排尚待交割后的整合。 拉美由此成为观察这笔收购影响的一个直接窗口。 福田在巴西的扩张正在加快。今年上半年，其当地上牌量达到1745辆，同比增长138%。公司已在南里奥格兰德州投产卡车组装线，并在伊塔雅伊经营配件配送中心。本地生产与售后投入伴随着销量增长，福田正在为更大的业务规模铺路。 福田的组装线和配件库，需要靠当地销量增长逐步消化投入。塔塔则有机会通过依维柯利用现成的网络。若塔塔的产品能够由这些渠道销售和维护，新集团扩大拉美业务时，就能减少重新铺设网点的投入。再叠加采购和研发降本，其让利空间可能扩大。中国企业仍在增加本地投入，原有对手一旦缩小车价差距，海外业务的利润就会承受更多压力。 欧洲客车市场的竞争更进一步，中国品牌已经站到了前排。 据行业媒体Sustainable Bus援引DVV统计，今年上半年，在涵盖欧盟、英国等市场的8吨以上纯电动巴士口径下，宇通注册量为1636辆，依维柯与Heuliez合计1156辆。两者争夺的已经是同一批电动化更新需求，塔塔入主后的整合效率，将影响依维柯继续争取订单的能力。 欧洲客户采购客车时，车辆与多年服务往往一同进入合同。依维柯2024年获得的罗马ATAC订单，除了411辆电动公交车，还包含十年全服务维护，由当地经销商提供维修车间及现场支持。整车制造成本如果下降，依维柯就有更多空间调整合同报价，而既有服务安排可以继续保留。 宇通也在增加这部分投入。今年9月，其欧洲首个综合服务中心在挪威斯托克开业，将交付、维修、配件和培训集中在一处，还配备了支持当地强制年检的设施。国内电动客车的开发和制造能力已经帮助宇通拿到订单，接下来的服务投入，则要让这些车辆在欧洲持续运营，也为客户下一轮采购建立信任。 在欧洲轻型商用车领域，依维柯还能通过金融服务争取客户。其经由IVECO CAPITAL提供的RENTIVE长期租赁，已把车辆、设备、维修及道路救援等服务组合起来。客户比较的是合同期内的用车支出，制造成本一旦下降，依维柯就有空间调整整套方案的报价。 不过，塔塔并没有拿到一份可以立即兑现的降本收益。 依维柯今年第二季度收入同比增长7.3%，调整后息税前利润却由上年同期的1.71亿欧元降至1.31亿欧元。公司将利润压力部分归因于产品质量投入及客车返工成本，同时表示相关客车返工已完成，预计下半年盈利逐步修复。 正式要约还保留了两年的非财务承诺，包括保留依维柯主要品牌、都灵总部及运营架构，两年内不进行重大重组或关闭工厂。塔塔需要在保留现有制造体系的前提下取得收益，采购和研发整合能节省多少，将直接影响这笔交易的回报。 中国供应链也会继续参与其中。依维柯今年10月获得的阿塞拜疆100辆小巴订单，将由南京依维柯组装；其2026款eDaily还增加了宁德时代磷酸铁锂电池方案。中国企业的制造和电池能力，已经成为这家欧洲车企海外业务的一部分。 塔塔若能把旗下产品接入依维柯网络，中国商用车将遇到一个更难绕开的对手。中国车企在欧洲、拉美的扩张，也将更多碰上同一家集团的连续应战。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 贝泰妮三季度扣非转亏，薇诺娜之外拓展婴童洗护与抗衰业务
articles.summary: 贝泰妮继续拓展婴童洗护与抗衰业务，第三季度收入和利润却出现回落。 10月26日晚，贝泰妮披露2026年三季报。第三季度，公司营收10.46亿元，同比下降4.28%；归母净利润1801.76万元，同比下降28.55%；扣非净利润亏损2319.47万元。 前三季度累计业绩仍保持增长，营收36.37亿元，同比增长4.99%；归母净利润3.10亿元，同比增长13.95%；扣非净利润2.23亿元，同比增长21.38%。不过，相比上半年归母净利润18.30%的增速，第三季度表现拉低了累计增长速度。 归母利润与扣非利润的差距，来自非经常性收益。第三季度，公司非经常性损益净额约4121万元，其中较大一项是金融资产公允价值变动等收益。这部分收益使当季归母净利润保持为正，扣非口径则显示出经营中的盈利压力。 压力主要体现在销售投入与收入的变化不匹配。根据三季报与半年报测算，第三季度销售费用约6.39亿元，同比增长15.47%；销售费用率由去年同期约50.65%升至61.10%。同期毛利率约74.71%，较去年同期有所改善，但销售费用率上升仍明显压缩了利润空间。 公司今年的业务拓展，正在向薇诺娜之外延伸。上半年，主品牌薇诺娜收入19.99亿元，同比增长2.54%，仍占主营收入近八成；薇诺娜宝贝、瑷科缦收入分别为1.69亿元、0.75亿元，同比增长54.04%和46%。子品牌增长更快，但规模与主品牌仍有较大差距。 薇诺娜宝贝正在增加家庭日常护理场景。7月，品牌在上海CBME孕婴童展上发布面向3岁以上儿童的洗沐系列，将产品从面霜、防晒等延伸至洗发、沐浴。增加清洁类产品，意味着品牌可以覆盖更多日常使用需求，也为母婴渠道增加可销售的品种。 瑷科缦则围绕专业护理与居家抗衰展开。公司8月披露，品牌已覆盖全国超过700家专业院线机构，通过院线服务建立专业认知，再连接消费者日常护肤需求。这条业务线与薇诺娜的敏感肌护理定位形成区分，也让贝泰妮接触到不同的消费人群。 渠道端，内容电商的重要性上升。上半年公司抖音渠道收入6.42亿元，同比增长57.38%，明显快于阿里系渠道。新平台带来了销售增量，也使直播、内容推广和用户运营成为经营中的重要投入。 第四季度的备货和推广已经提前启动。三季度末，公司存货7.58亿元，较年初增加43.42%；预付款项1.57亿元，较年初增加77.47%。公司解释，存货增加主要为第四季度大促和新品上市备货，预付款增加则主要对应直播、种草、平台推广及广告营销安排。 年末销售旺季到来前，库存和营销资源已先行投入，接下来需要销售增长来消化。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
